from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient adjunction: the diagonal/coherent comparison. Rezk, Fibrations and Homotopy Colimits of Simplicial Sheaves, Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 2.2, for sharpness of the diagonal of an equifibered simplicial object.

title: Rezk diagonal sharpness for equifibered simplicial diagrams
statement: Use small simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the Kan--Quillen model structure from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A commutative square is homotopy cartesian when its upper-left corner maps by a weak homotopy equivalence to the homotopy pullback of the other three corners; for non-Kan objects this is computed after functorial fibrant replacement of the diagram. Call a map $g:E\to B$ sharp if every strict pullback square along every small simplicial map $A\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be simplicial diagrams and $p:X\to Y$ a natural transformation. Suppose each $p_m:X_m\to Y_m$ is sharp and every naturality square for an operator $[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$ is homotopy cartesian. Put $(\operatorname{diag}Z)_q=(Z_q)_q$ for $Z=X,Y$, with both operators applied simultaneously. Then $\operatorname{diag}p$ is sharp. Neither the rows nor the diagonals are required to be Kan, and no Reedy fibrancy is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 6.1, printed pp. 11-12; Proposition 2.7, printed p. 4, identifies the definition of sharpness with universal homotopy-cartesianness. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.
